thread:
maria: quick note — saw repeated tail latency spikes today on the inference shard (p95->p99 jumps). nsys timeline shows bursts of cudaMalloc/cudaFree clustered around KV-cache refill windows. publishing the capture shortly. :frowning_face:

devin: can you paste the nsys CLI you used? and the short timeline snippet if possible?

maria: ran with:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/malloc_trace --trace=nvtx,cuda --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi ./start-loadtest.sh
```

timeline view (condensed):
```
[00:01:12.432] kernel_matmul (fast path)
[00:01:12.497] cudaMalloc (12ms)
[00:01:12.513] kernel_attention
[00:01:12.521] cudaFree (8ms)
[00:01:12.612] cudaMalloc (9ms)
... (repeats when many concurrent requests hit cold KV entries)
```

maria: note the cudaMalloc spikes are not GPU kernel hotspots but host-side blocking allocations — they push a few batches over the latency SLO.

siva: that smells like a thundering-herd on KV cache refill. are we allocating small chunks per-KV-entry or doing many tiny arenas? what allocator are we using now?

maria: default cudaMalloc, per-request small allocations for KV cache nodes (object ~2KB to 64KB). we tried a basic pooling wrapper earlier but not in this build.

devin: try sampling to get stack traces for cudaMalloc callers — use the env var NVTX ranges + nsys with cudaProfilerApi range markers around the request path. also enable `CUDA_MEMPOOL` feature if available for the driver.

jess: perf-bot ran a 10m comparison earlier this week on a similar workload:
```
perf-bot: prepool: ~1200 cudaMalloc calls / min, avg malloc time 7.6ms
perf-bot: with slab-pool: ~18 cudaMalloc calls / min, avg malloc time 0.9ms
perf-bot: p99 latency improved ~45% on that shard
```

maria: thanks — curious if those numbers hold for our larger sequence-length profiles. I'll run a targeted nvtx-instrumented trace of the KV refill path with concurrency 80.

siva: also add `cudaMemGetInfo` logs before/after allocation to verify fragmentation free bytes. sometimes fragmentation looks fine overall but allocation fails and triggers slow fallback.

maria: good call. snippet I'm adding to the code for trace builds:
```cpp
nvtxRangePushA("kv-refill");
size_t free_before, total_before; cudaMemGetInfo(&free_before, &total_before);
void* p; cudaMalloc(&p, size);
size_t free_after, total_after; cudaMemGetInfo(&free_after, &total_after);
nvtxRangePop();
LOG_INFO("malloc size=%zu free_before=%zu free_after=%zu", size, free_before, free_after);
```

devin: if we still see many small allocations we should try two experiments in parallel: 1) a per-worker slab (bump size to 32MB) with reuse, 2) a driver mempool/heap configured with large preallocated arenas. measure malloc call count and avg malloc latency.

maria: ran quick A/B locally: slab-per-worker (32MB) reduced cudaMalloc count from ~980/min -> 22/min and brought average malloc latency down from 8ms -> 1.1ms. however, noticed occasional long pauses when slab was exhausted and we fell back to cudaMalloc — need better backpressure.

siva: that's expected. set high-water mark and block acceptor threads until slab has 64KB free, or pre-expand slab on hotspot detection. also add an eviction strategy that async-frees to a recycler thread to avoid blocking request threads.

jess: ops-bot: rolling trace job queued on prod-sim-3 cluster with nvtx and meminfo logging, run-id=20260312-22. estimated 40m.

ops-bot: job queued: id=20260312-22, target=prod-sim-3, tags=[nsys,nvtx,kv-refill], ETA 40m. notify @maria when done.

maria: thanks. one more datapoint: kernel selection interplay — when small allocations block, continuous-batching windows sometimes collapse and a different matmul kernel gets chosen (one optimized for shorter seqs) which increases cost. so the allocator behavior has knock-on effects beyond pure latency.

devin: good call — include a timeline of kernel names alongside malloc events in the trace so we can correlate kernel-switch times with allocation stalls. nsys timeline + name labels (from our kernel telemetry) will show it.

siva: long-term: we should instrument model runtime to prefer pre-warming KV entries during off-peak, and make pool growth asynchronous. short-term: implement per-worker slab + recycler thread and add NVTX around pool alloc/free to make traces clearer.

maria: I'll run the prod-sim job and post the trace file + short summary. next steps: (1) per-worker slab with async recycler in feature branch, (2) nvtx-instrumented capture of kernel timeline + meminfo, (3) automated test that simulates KV churn at concurrency 100 to catch regressions.

devin: :thumbsup: please tag this thread when you upload the capture. if results look good we'll schedule a small canary rollout behind our fallback policy.

maria: uploaded results to the trace bucket: s3://redwood-traces/prod-sim-3/20260312-22/{nsys.qdrep,summary.txt}. summary: prepool p99=390ms, postpool p99=220ms; cudaMalloc/min 1120 -> 20. attaching short CSV of malloc samples and stack hashes.

siva: excellent — can you add the stack-hash -> top frame mapping (we need to know whether allocator calls originate from kv.c/kv_node_create or some higher-level buffer)?

maria: yes will add. thanks all, this explains the intermittent latency regressions we've been chasing. follow-up PR incoming with slab + recycler and NVTX markers. :white_check_mark:
